subject: chemistry
question_text: What are Lewis dot symbols? What is their significance?

verification.note: PREDICTED, not asked. This question comes from the enumeration sweep: Lewis dot symbols open the NCERT Chemical Bonding chapter, and the Fastrack chemistry section (book pp.56-61) skips the section entirely. Only ONE source book is held for chemistry — the TSBIE Basic Learning Material in hand covers physics only — so the two-book union check is PENDING a second chemistry source. The 1+1 mark split is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: What they are
lines: Lewis dot symbols show the valence
electrons of an atom as dots placed around
Ex: nitrogen has five valence electrons,
so its Lewis symbol shows five dots
steps.why: The symbol is a counting device: only the outermost electrons take part in bonding, so only they are drawn.
common_mistakes: Drawing ALL the electrons as dots. Only the valence (outermost) electrons are shown.
Writing the number of dots equal to the atomic number.
steps.memory_tip: Dots equal the outer electrons only — for nitrogen, five.
steps.margin_note: One sentence plus one named example is the full mark.

steps.label: Significance

lines.text: The number of dots equals the valence electrons

lines: The symbols are used to count the electrons
available for bonding and to show how atoms
complete an octet by losing, gaining or
steps.why: The significance is the use: the dots make octet counting visible, which is the basis of every Lewis structure in this chapter.
common_mistakes: Stopping at the definition. The significance sentence — counting bonding electrons — is the second mark.
steps.memory_tip: The dots show what the atom can lose, gain or share in bonding.

insider_note: Two questions, one mark each, and the significance is the half students leave out. Say what the dots let you count, not only what they are.
